newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia targets nine tech sectors for new bourse.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia targets nine tech sectors for new bourse.

text.p: Malaysia is targeting nine technology-linked industries for listings on its proposed MESDAQ stock exchange set to be launched early next year, the exchange planners said on Monday.

"Companies with activities in these Priority Technology Areas will be accorded a priority status for listing on MESDAQ," said Nazir Razak, who chairs a securities industry committee to spearhead the formation of the Malaysian Exchange of Securities Dealing and Automated Quotation Bhd (MESDAQ).
He told reporters at a briefing that the focus on the nine areas does not mean MESDAQ will not consider other sectors such as high-growth and small- and medium-sized enterprises.
But listing applications from companies not in the priority areas will be put on the backburner if there are other firms which meet the criteria also seeking to list at the same time, he said.

The nine priority areas are: advanced electronics and information technology, equipment/instrumentation automation and flexible manufacturing systems, as well as biotechnology, bio-conversion and genetic engineering.
The other six areas are electro-optics, non-linear optics and opto-electronics; advanced materials, energy source, aerospace, transportation and services sectors.

The proposed exchange for high-technology, high-growth companies is on schedule to be launched in the fourth quarter of this year with trading for the market-maker based system expected in the first quarter of next year, Nazir said.

Modelled on the highly-successful NASDAQ exchange in the United States that counts scores of technology and emerging growth firms as its members, MESDAQ is also targeted at developing Malaysia's Multimedia Super Corridor (MSC).
The MSC, a test-bed for multimedia applications, is a 15-by-50 km (9-by-30 mile) corridor south of Malaysia's capital of Kuala Lumpur.
Companies seeking listing do not need to have a profit record but must have a minimum two million ringgit ($757,600) share capital.
He said the MESDAQ-listed firms are different from infrastructure project companies (IPC) on the Kuala lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) whose earnings stream is predictable.
"(Earnings are) too predictable for IPC companies. Whereas MESDAQ is quite at the other end of the spectrum. It can bomb or it can really grow exponetially," he said.
Malaysia's KLSE already has a main board of large, blue chip companies, as well as a small-capitalisation Second Board.

On MESDAQ possibly representing an opportunity for stock price manipulation, Nazir said the exchange's full disclosure-based regulation will create transparency. "Speculation we will always have, manipulation we hope to mitigate," he said.
